finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route returns any invoice to any caller with no authentication or ownership check (IDOR / broken access control). The sibling /my/invoice route does check ownership, so this route is inconsistent with it.
finding.source: Any HTTP client supplies inv_id in the URL path. No login is needed because the route does not reference g.user.
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at line 10 returns the full invoice record, including the customer field and other invoice data.

trace.note: Route is registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) fetches the record by the attacker-supplied ID, or aborts with 404.
The record is returned without comparing inv['customer'] to g.user['id'].

finding.guards_checked: Searched the only file in the repo for a before_request hook, auth decorator, or ownership check on this route and found none. The file does not define g.user at all, so any auth middleware would have to be elsewhere, and no other files exist. Even if such middleware existed, it would only authenticate, not check per-invoice ownership. I could not tell whether the route was meant as an admin endpoint, but nothing in the code restricts it to admins.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no auth decorator, before_request hook, or ownership check and returns jsonify(inv), while the sibling route at invoices.py:16 checks inv["customer"] against g.user["id"]; invoices.py is the only file in the repo, so no other control exists.
